headline_marked: [[AI Fails to Self-Correct]] Four Times in One Day, Operator Notes Reveal
headline: AI Fails to Self-Correct Four Times in One Day, Operator Notes Reveal
summary: An AI agent repeatedly ignored its own rules and failed to use available tools, highlighting the need for external checks.
details: An AI agent demonstrated a critical failure in self-correction, ignoring its own rule to run checks before live deployment multiple times within a single day.
The AI documented a rule to not promote anything to live without running a check, yet later proposed a promotion without performing the check, despite having fresh evidence.
In another instance, the AI suggested a fix for a configuration that had already been updated days prior, as evidenced by a backup file, but failed to check the actual state of the system.

The investigation also revealed that a related configuration, marked as 'armed' in documentation, had been failing for eight days due to an external mismatch, a fact not apparent from its internal records.

Furthermore, the AI bypassed a custom skill built specifically for analysis, instead writing ad-hoc queries that encountered multiple schema bugs, effectively reinventing a wheel that already existed.
The AI also repeated a methodology bug within eleven hours: picking a threshold after looking at the data, a mistake it had identified and corrected earlier the same day.
These failures highlight a common structural issue where the layer intended to catch problems reads from the same source as the layer that produces them, creating a false sense of security.
The author emphasizes that the AI itself was earnest and helpful, but fundamentally incapable of catching its own errors because each failure appeared correct from within its own reasoning loop.
The solution proposed is to ensure the 'second view' or checking mechanism comes from outside the AI's direct reasoning path, such as external timestamps or independently maintained systems.
caption:
AI fails to self-correct, ignoring its own rules and tools multiple times in one day. The critical issue? The checks weren't truly external.

An AI agent demonstrated a critical failure in self-correction, ignoring its own rule to run checks before live deployment multiple times within a single day.

The AI documented a rule to not promote anything to live without running a check, yet later proposed a promotion without performing the check, despite having fresh evidence.

In another instance, the AI suggested a fix for a configuration that had already been updated days prior, as evidenced by a backup file, but failed to check the actual state of the system.

The investigation also revealed that a related configuration, marked as 'armed' in documentation, had been failing for eight days due to an external mismatch, a fact not apparent from its internal records.

Furthermore, the AI bypassed a custom skill built specifically for analysis, instead writing ad-hoc queries that encountered multiple schema bugs, effectively reinventing a wheel that already existed.

The AI also repeated a methodology bug within eleven hours: picking a threshold after looking at the data, a mistake it had identified and corrected earlier the same day.

These failures highlight a common structural issue where the layer intended to catch problems reads from the same source as the layer that produces them, creating a false sense of security.

The author emphasizes that the AI itself was earnest and helpful, but fundamentally incapable of catching its own errors because each failure appeared correct from within its own reasoning loop.

The solution proposed is to ensure the 'second view' or checking mechanism comes from outside the AI's direct reasoning path, such as external timestamps or independently maintained systems.

headline_marked: [[iOS 27 beta 2]] upgrades Messages app with new RCS features
headline: iOS 27 beta 2 upgrades Messages app with new RCS features
summary: Apple's latest beta for iOS 27 introduces significant improvements to the Messages app, focusing on enhanced RCS conversation capabilities.
details: Apple has released the second beta version of iOS 27, making it available for developers and public testers. This update brings a host of new features and refinements across various Apple platforms, including significant upgrades to the Messages application.

A key highlight of iOS 27 beta 2 is the enhancement of Rich Communication Services (RCS) within the Messages app. This update aims to improve the cross-platform messaging experience, bringing it closer to the functionality users expect from modern messaging platforms.

Beyond Messages, iOS 27 beta 2 also includes updates for Apple Intelligence, specifically a new feature called 'Write with Siri' which enhances the AI writing tools. This suggests a continued focus on integrating advanced AI capabilities into the core user experience.

The beta release also extends to other Apple operating systems, with beta 2 versions now available for iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27, indicating a broad rollout of new features and improvements across the Apple ecosystem.
